raw_case_text: A 13-month-old male child from Koraput district, Orissa, was diagnosed to have malaria with smear positive for PF. He was treated with a 3-day course of oral artesunate-SP. In view of persistent fever and failure of parasite clearance after 3 days, he was administered second course of 3 days oral artesunate-SP. He was referred to our hospital in view of severe anemia and persistence of ring forms of PF in blood smear. He was started on parenteral quinine along with clindamycin and a dose of primaquine was administered. Serial peripheral smears were performed which showed parasitological clearance after 48 h of initiating therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 13-month-old male child from Koraput district, Odisha, India, was referred with persistent fever and severe anemia after failing two 3-day courses of oral artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed locally with smear-positive Plasmodium falciparum malaria, the infant received a 3-day course of oral artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (SP) followed by a second 3-day oral artesunate-SP course due to persistent fever and parasitemia, and was referred for severe anemia and refractory parasitemia.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resident of Koraput district, Odisha (malaria-endemic area); received two consecutive 3-day courses of oral artesunate-SP.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent fever and pallor/anemia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine-refractory Plasmodium falciparum malaria with severe anemia. Referral peripheral blood smear confirmed persistent P. falciparum ring forms. Treated with parenteral quinine plus clindamycin and a single gametocytocidal dose of primaquine, achieving documented parasitological clearance on serial peripheral smears after 48 hours of therapy.
